{{short description|Argentinian physicist, specialized in computational physics}}
'''Mariana Weissmann''' (born 17 December 1933) is an Argentinian physicist, specializing in the computational physics of condensed matter. In 2003, Weissmann became the first Argentinian scientist to receive the [[L'Oréal-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science|L'Oréal-UNESCO Award to Women in Science]].<ref>{{cite web|title = La vida secreta de los sonidos|url = http://www.lanacion.com.ar/992734-la-vida-secreta-de-los-sonidos|website = www.lanacion.com.ar|accessdate = 2015-11-08|first = Valeria|last = Shapira|date = 9 March 2008|publisher = La Nación|archive-date = 2017-12-03|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171203153823/http://www.lanacion.com.ar/992734-la-vida-secreta-de-los-sonidos|url-status = dead}}</ref> The same year she received the [[Konex Award|Prize Konex]] in Physics.

== Work ==
Weissmann received her PhD in 1965 at the [[University of Buenos Aires]] and she did her postgraduate studies at the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Mariana Weissmann|url = http://www.ianas.org/index.php/programs/women-for-science/working-group/79-members/460-mariana-weissmann|website = Inter-American Network of Academies of Sciences|accessdate = 2015-11-08|archive-date = 2015-10-24|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151024164340/http://www.ianas.org/index.php/programs/women-for-science/working-group/79-members/460-mariana-weissmann|url-status = dead}}</ref> She specialized in theoretical studies and [[Computer simulation|numerical simulations]] of the properties of [[Solid-state physics|solid state]].<ref name="KONEX">{{Cite web|url= http://www.fundacionkonex.com.ar/b2483-mariana_weissmann|title= Mariana Weissmann - Premio Konex 200|author= Fundación Konex|year= 2003|accessdate= 2014-06-12|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140714150909/http://www.fundacionkonex.com.ar/b2483-mariana_weissmann|archive-date= 2014-07-14|url-status= dead}}</ref><ref name="CLARIN">{{Cite news|url = http://old.clarin.com/diario/2003/02/27/s-03001.htm|title= Una física argentina ganó un importante premio internacional|journal= Clarín|date= 27 February 2003|accessdate= 2014-06-12}}</ref>

Her works on computational physics of condensed matter in the formation of [[ice]] opened up the possibility of [[cloud seeding]] to change the amount or type of precipitation that falls from clouds.<ref name="CLARIN"/><ref>{{Cite journal|title = On the hydrogen bond in an ice-like structure|journal = Chemical Physics Letters|date = 1967-05-01|pages = 95–98|volume = 1|issue = 3|doi = 10.1016/0009-2614(67)85032-2|first = Mariana|last = Weissmann|first2 = L.|last2 = Blum|first3 = Norah V.|last3 = Cohan|bibcode = 1967CPL.....1...95W}}</ref> She also studied [[silicon]] surfaces and their interaction with [[Carbon|atoms of carbon]]. This included recently discovered molecules like doped [[fullerene]]s doped.<ref name="KONEX"/>

She has directed numerous PhDs and published more than 100 scientific publications in international journals.<ref name="KONEX"/>

In 2003, she received the [[L'Oréal-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science]] in their category of [[Latin America]], the first Argentine scientist to receive the award which was created in 1998.<ref name="KONEX"/><ref name="CLARIN"/>
